details: ID: c36a81df-2b1c-4abe-b492-2a5564005540, Name: Parametric, Type: MathGuide
Message: We already know that explicit representations let us compute points using formulas like y = x² - 5., ContentType: OnlyText, Interaction: Continue
ID: ab991f0e-7d91-45f8-af87-8b379bccdfb4, Name: Explicit, Type: MathGuide
Message: Hey there, in this part we’re going to explore how to define a set of points explicitly., ContentType: OnlyText, Interaction: Continue
Message: An explicit representation can be as simple as listing the points in the set., ContentType: OnlyText, Interaction: Continue
Message: For example: {[0,0], [1,2], [2,4], [3,6]} is a set of four points., ContentType: Geometry, Interaction: Continue
Message: Another, more interesting, way is to specify a formula or rule that generates each point in a set., ContentType: OnlyText, Interaction: Continue

Message: For example, the explicit representation of a linear function can look like this 
{[x, y] | y = x + 2}., ContentType: OnlyText, Interaction: Continue
Message: Notice that the condition expresses y directly in terms of x., ContentType: OnlyText, Interaction: Continue
